# MDEdit

> MDEdit is a native Markdown editor for macOS 14 or later. It opens a folder as a project and edits the plain .md and .txt files in it directly. Notes are never imported into a library or database.

## What it does

- Opens any folder as a binder (sidebar tree) of notes and subfolders; rename, move, trash and drop files in from Finder.
- Write mode shows the Markdown, lightly styled as you type. View mode sets the same note in a serif or sans reading typeface.
- Wiki links ([[Note]], [[Note|alias]], [[Note#Heading]], [[folder/Note]]), backlinks, an outline panel, and front matter shown as a properties table.
- Find and replace in one note or across the whole folder, with a diff preview and one undo.
- Opens HTML, JSON and YAML files as code. Preview shows an HTML page, pretty-printed JSON, or YAML as a table. HTML files with template tags can build index pages from the notes in the folder (read-only).
- Runs in the macOS sandbox, saves as you type, refuses to overwrite files changed on disk by something else, keeps a copy of unsaved work if saving fails.
- Optional local agent server (off by default): an AI agent can read the open note and propose edits over MCP; each suggestion shows as a diff in a Review tab and nothing changes until the user accepts it.
- No account, no sync service, no tracking; makes no network connections of its own.

## Facts

- Platform: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Mac only.
- Download: https://github.com/satran/mdedit/releases/latest/download/MDEdit.dmg
- All releases: https://github.com/satran/mdedit/releases/latest
- Author: Satyajit Ranjeev
- Home page: https://mdedit.ranjeev.in/
